4
A snooker ball of mass 0.20 kg has a collision so that its direction of movement changes by an
angle of 90°, as shown.
0.30 m s–1
snooker ball,
mass 0.20 kg
0.40 m s–1
before the collision
after the collision
The ball has a speed of 0.40 m s–1 before the collision and a speed of 0.30 m s–1 after the collision.
What is the magnitude of the change in momentum of the snooker ball?
A
0.020 kg m s–1
B
0.10 kg m s–1
C
0.14 kg m s–1
D
0.50 kg m s–1

hints: Notice the before arrow is $0.40 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ to the right and the after arrow is $0.30 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ upwards, so the two momentum vectors are at $90^\circ$.
Recall momentum $p = mv$ is a vector, so change in momentum is $\Delta p = p_{after} - p_{before}$ found by vector subtraction, not $m$ times speed difference.
Calculate the two magnitudes $0.20 \times 0.40$ and $0.20 \times 0.30$, then use Pythagoras for the right-angled triangle to get $|\Delta p|$.
walkthrough: Identify the vectors from the diagram: before, $v = 0.40 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ to the right; after, $v = 0.30 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ upwards. Mass is $m = 0.20 \text{ kg}$.
State the rule: momentum $p = mv$ is a vector, so $\Delta p = p_{after} - p_{before}$ must be done by vector subtraction.
Calculate each momentum magnitude: $p_{before} = 0.20 \times 0.40 = 0.080 \text{ kg m s}^{-1}$ and $p_{after} = 0.20 \times 0.30 = 0.060 \text{ kg m s}^{-1}$.
Because the change of direction is $90^\circ$, $p_{before}$, $p_{after}$ and $\Delta p$ form a right-angled triangle with $\Delta p$ as the hypotenuse.
Use Pythagoras: $|\Delta p| = \sqrt{p_{before}^2 + p_{after}^2} = \sqrt{0.080^2 + 0.060^2} = \sqrt{0.0100} = 0.10 \text{ kg m s}^{-1}$.

A.explanation: This subtracts the speeds as scalars, $0.20 \times (0.40 - 0.30)$, and ignores the 90-degree change of direction shown in the diagram.

B.explanation: The perpendicular momenta $0.080$ and $0.060 \text{ kg m s}^{-1}$ give a vector change of $\sqrt{0.080^2 + 0.060^2} = 0.10 \text{ kg m s}^{-1}$.

C.explanation: This adds the momentum magnitudes as scalars, $0.080 + 0.060 = 0.14 \text{ kg m s}^{-1}$, instead of subtracting them as perpendicular vectors.

D.explanation: This is the magnitude of the velocity change, $\sqrt{0.40^2 + 0.30^2} = 0.50 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, without multiplying by the $0.20 \text{ kg}$ mass.
